Tosafot on Bava Batra 119a:2:1.english: "And through the merit of the father of their mothers" - This is where, for example, the father of their mothers had no sons, only daughters, for if not, the sons would inherit. And if you ask: But who returned [the inheritance] to them? One can answer: For example, where they were brothers of the father of their mothers, who had sons, and the sons returned [the inheritance] to their fathers, and they divided it equally.

Tosafot on Bava Batra 119a:3:1.hebrew: הא דהוו בני עשרים כו' - בבניהם אי אתה מוצא שלא היו בני עשרים, כמו שפירש בקונטרס, דבליעת קרח נמי היתה מיד אחר המרגלים, כמו שהביא מסדר עולם דקתני: אחר ביאת מרגלים היתה בליעת קרח. ואם לא שסמוך היה, מאי קא משמע לן? וכן משמע נמי מדאמרי: "הן גוענו כולנו אבדנו" (במדבר יז), ומתרגם: הא מיננא קטלית חרבא, הא מיננא בליעת ארעא, הא מיננא מתו במותנא — ששלשה מעשים הללו היו רצופין, מדמדכרי להו אהדדי. וקטלת חרבא היינו מעשה מרגלים, כדכתיב (שם יד): "ויכום ויכתום" וגו'. ואין להקשות: אמאי הוצרך לומר "בזכות אבי אביהן"? לימא "בזכות אביהן" ממש, דהיינו בני מרגלים ובני המתלוננים עצמן! דהאי תנא אתא לאשמועינן דאפילו אותן שלא נטלו מחמת עצמן, שלא היו בני כ' כשבאו לארץ, ולא נטלו נמי בזכות אבותיהן ממש — כגון שמתו במדבר — ולא נטלו נמי ע"י חזרה, שלא נולדו להן שום בן שהיה בן עשרים, אפילו הכי נטלו בזכות אבי אביהן, אע"פ שבא להן מחמת מרגלים ומתלוננים. וא"ת: אמאי לא קאמר "הא והא ליוצאי מצרים, והא כשהיו אביהן ממש בני מרגלים ומתלוננים בני עשרים כשיצאו ממצרים", דהיינו מחמת עצמן, שלא בא להן מכח מרגלים ומתלוננים? והא דקאמר "בזכות אבי אביהן" — שלא היו אבותיהן בני עשרים ביציאת מצרים. ובשלמא אי הוה אמר דבניהן ממש של מרגלים ושל מתלוננים עצמן מיירי הכא שבאו לארץ, הוה אתי שפיר דלא הוה מצי למימר "הא והא ליוצאי מצרים, והא והא דהוו בני עשרים כשיצאו", דאם כן איך באו לארץ? דבני עשרים כולן מתו במדבר. ויש לומר דהשתא נמי דאיירי בבני בניהם לא מצי לשנויי הכי, דמשמע נמי דבאי הארץ נטלו בזכות עצמן, ולא שאבותיהן נחלו והורישו להן:
Tosafot on Bava Batra 119a:3:1.english: "That they were twenty years old," etc. - In their sons you do not find that they were not twenty years old, as [Rashi] explained in the Kuntres, for the swallowing of Korach too was immediately after the [episode of the] spies, as he cited from Seder Olam, which teaches: After the coming of the spies was the swallowing of Korach. And if it were not adjacent, what would it be teaching us? And so it is also implied from what they said: "Behold, we perish, we are lost, we are all lost" (Numbers 17), and [Targum] translates: "Behold, some of us were killed by the sword; behold, some of us [were lost through] the swallowing of the earth; behold, some of us died by plague" — that these three events were consecutive, since they mention them together. And "killed by the sword" refers to the incident of the spies, as it is written (ibid. 14): "And they smote them and beat them down," etc. And one should not ask: Why did it need to say "in the merit of their father's father"? Let it say "in the merit of their father" literally, meaning the sons of the spies and of the complainers themselves! [The answer is that] this Tanna comes to teach us that even those who did not take on their own account, because they were not twenty years old when they came to the land, and also did not take in the merit of their actual fathers — for example, because [their fathers] died in the wilderness — and also did not take through reversion, because no son who was twenty years old was born to them, even so they took in the merit of their father's father, even though [the inheritance] came to them by way of the spies and the complainers. And if you ask: Why does it not say, "This and this refer to those who left Egypt, and this [other case is] where their actual fathers, the sons of the spies and complainers, were twenty years old when they left Egypt," that is, on their own account, such that it did not come to them by virtue of the spies and complainers? And what it says, "in the merit of their father's father," would mean that their fathers were not twenty at the Exodus from Egypt. Now, granted, if it had said that it is speaking here of the actual sons of the spies and complainers themselves, who came to the land, it would be well that it could not have said, "This and this refer to those who left Egypt, and this and this [refers to] those who were twenty when they left," for if so, how did they come to the land? For all those twenty years old and above died in the wilderness. But one can say that now too, since it is speaking of their grandchildren, it could not answer this way, since it would also imply that those who came to the land took in their own right, and not that their fathers had inherited and bequeathed it to them.

Tosafot on Bava Batra 119a:5:1.hebrew: מתיב רבה רבי יהודה אומר בנות צלפחד נטלו ארבעה חלקים שנאמר ויפלו חבלי מנשה עשרה - וקרא ע"כ לא איירי ביתדות ואהלים אלא בחלוקה. וליכא למימר דלמא תלתא אחי דאבא הוו להו, דאז לא הוו בהו שום חדוש, דהא חלק בכורה לא נטלו; וא"כ לא הוה ליה לקרא לאחשובינהו, אלא דבתי אבות גרידא, כדפריך רב פפא לעיל: אי טפלים קא חשיב, טובא הוו:
Tosafot on Bava Batra 119a:5:1.english: Rabbah objected: Rabbi Yehuda says the daughters of Tzelofchad took four portions, as it is stated: "And there fell ten portions to Manasseh" - And the verse, necessarily, is not speaking of tent pegs and tents, but of the division [of the land]. And one cannot say that perhaps [Tzelofchad] had three brothers [i.e., the daughters' paternal uncles], for then there would be nothing novel about them, since they did not take the firstborn's portion; and if so, the verse should have counted only the fathers' houses alone, as Rav Papa asks above: If it is counting the secondary ones, there are many more.

Tosafot on Bava Batra 119a:6:1.hebrew: יודע היה משה שבנות צלפחד יורשות הן - אע"פ שלא נאמרה פרשת נחלה, יודע היה משה מטעם דלקמן: "אם כבן אנו נירש, אם כבת תתייבם אמנו":
Tosafot on Bava Batra 119a:6:1.english: Moses knew that the daughters of Tzelofchad inherit - Even though the passage of inheritance had not yet been stated, Moses knew [this] from the reasoning given below: "If we are treated like a son, we will inherit; if like a daughter, our mother should be taken in levirate marriage."

Tosafot on Bava Batra 119a:8:1.hebrew: שנאמר מחלליה מות יומת, אבל לא היה יודע באיזו מיתה נהרג - ואם תאמר: למה היה מסתפק? היה לו לדונו בחנק, דכל מיתה האמורה בתורה סתם — חנק! ויש לומר: דמסברא היה נראה לו שנדון בסקילה כעובד ע"ז, דבכל דוכתא (חולין ה.) אמר דדומה שבת לע"ז, דהיינו מחלל שבת בפרהסיא, לעובד ע"ז. וצריך לומר דסבר כרבנן ולא כר"י, דאי כר' יהודה דאמר באלו הן הנשרפין (סנהדרין דף פ:) "עד שיודיעוהו באיזו מיתה הוא נהרג", דלדידיה אמר התם דהוראת שעה היתה (דאם) כן לא ידע משה שדינו במיתה:
Tosafot on Bava Batra 119a:8:1.english: "As it is stated: 'Those who desecrate it shall surely be put to death'; but he did not know by which death he was to be executed" - And if you ask: Why was he uncertain? He should have judged him to strangulation, for any death stated in the Torah without specification is strangulation! And one can answer: That by reasoning it seemed to him that he would be judged to stoning, like an idol worshipper, for in many places (Chullin 5a) it says that Shabbat is comparable to idolatry — that is, one who desecrates Shabbat publicly is like an idol worshipper. And we must say that he held like the Rabbis and not like Rabbi Yehuda; for if [he held] like Rabbi Yehuda, who says in the chapter "Elu Hen HaNisrafin" (Sanhedrin 80b), "until they inform him by which death he is to be executed" — for according to him it is stated there that it was a temporary ruling ((for if) so, Moshe would not have known that his sentence was death).
